findings.reason: A cost-history update picture materially clarifies the distinction between one physical state and increasing finite-horizon risk. A compressed two-layer history graph shows the seven-decision tree without 128 leaves; the original standalone screenshot has no such explanation. This is a warranted explanatory addition, not a claim that the existing proof is incomplete.

diagram_math_checks.data: N_t means no risky action among first t decisions; H_t means at least one. These partition action histories; both retain physical CMDP state s.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Original Example line 31 and Given line 41 specify one physical state with deterministic self-transition, and cost 1 exactly on risky actions. New labels explicitly describe history events rather than new CMDP states.

diagram_math_checks.relation: N_t -> N_(t+1) has weight 9/10, N_t -> H_(t+1) has weight 1/10; H_t -> H_(t+1) has weight 1. H_t -> N_(t+1) has weight zero and is omitted.
diagram_math_checks.justification: The original independent safe/risky draws have probabilities 9/10 and 1/10. A risky draw first creates the hit flag; once a risky draw has occurred either next action leaves the hit flag set. Each outgoing update distribution sums to 1, with all arrows pointing forward in decision count. These are update rules, avoiding conditioning on the null H_0 event.

diagram_math_checks.relation: Pr(N_0)=1, Pr(H_0)=0; after seven updates Pr(N_7)=(9/10)^7 and Pr(H_7)=1-(9/10)^7>1/2.
diagram_math_checks.justification: No decisions at t=0 means no risky draw. Repeated independent safe factors give the original step 3.1 calculation; 10^7-9^7=5217031>5000000. The figure asserts no additional trajectory-cost bound.

Original steps 1.1 and 2.1 use one-step expected cost 1/10 and discount 1/10, as defined in local def-discounted-cost-constraint. The diagram counts finite histories and does not replace this infinite discounted-sum verification.
